data.body:
## RCA — the original description's premise was wrong; corrected mechanism below

I filed this asserting "there appears to be no retention bound (count, age, or total
size) and no cleanup on gate completion". **That is false.** Retention exists, is
deployed on the affected host, and ran during the incident window. Correcting the
record before anyone implements against the wrong premise.

### What actually exists

`src/rebar/_snapshot/janitor.py` (519 LOC) + `src/rebar/_snapshot/gc_trigger.py`
(244 LOC) implement exactly this reclamation, and `gc_trigger.py`'s docstring
describes a prior host that reached **64,021 entries / 47.24 GiB** — filed and
**closed** as bug `58a3-0756-e470-4b40` (`undamaged-epidermic-kakarikis`,
"Snapshot janitor runs only in the review-bot process; every other host…"). Its fix
— an operation-linked GC trigger keyed to gate resolution rather than to a daemon or
a CI provider — is live here and **working**: `<store>/gc/last-pass.stamp` carries
mtime `2026-08-26 19:07:20`, and the entry count fell 14,705 → 13,056 across that
pass.

### The actual defect: the reclamation axes cannot engage on this host

`JanitorConfig` reclaims along disk-pressure and age. Measured defaults
(`janitor.py:65-69`) against this host:

| Axis | Default | Engages here? |
|---|---|---|
| `free_watermark_bytes` | 2 GiB | **No** — 886 GiB free |
| `free_watermark_pct` | `0` (off) | **No** |
| `max_bytes` | `0` (off, opt-in) | **No** |
| `max_age_seconds` | 7 days | **Barely** — see below |
| **entry count** | **does not exist** | **N/A** |

Volume: 1.8 TiB, 886 GiB available, **51% capacity**. Nowhere near the 2 GiB floor,
and the percentage term and byte backstop both default off.

That leaves the 7-day cold-trim as the only live axis. Sampling 400 of the 13,056
entries by mtime: **every one falls between 2026-08-18 and 2026-08-26** — inside the
7-day window. A host that generates snapshots faster than they age out therefore
accumulates without bound, which is precisely why the 19:07 pass reclaimed only
~1,650 entries and stopped.

### Why the design misses it

Every existing axis measures **bytes or free space**. The harm here was neither: it
was **filesystem metadata pressure**. 13,000+ directories in one tree drove
`fseventsd` to 26.3 GB RSS and >150% CPU, exhausting swap (53,556 MB of 54,272 MB)
and pushing load average to 58 on a 6-performance-core host until applications could
not launch. Disk usage was never the binding constraint and no byte-denominated
threshold would have fired.

### Corrected scope

This is **not** a duplicate of `58a3` — that bug was "the janitor never runs outside
the review-bot", and its fix works. This is the distinct, still-live gap: **no
entry-count axis, and the byte/free-space axes are inert on a large, mostly-empty
volume.** Linking `relates_to 58a3` rather than `duplicates`.

The acceptance criteria in the description need rewriting accordingly — AC 1's
"enforces a retention bound" is already satisfied along three axes; the real
requirement is a **count-denominated** bound (or an equivalent metadata-pressure
proxy) that engages independently of disk headroom. AC 2/3/6 (cleanup on completion,
crash-leak reclamation, concurrency safety) are likewise already implemented by
`run_gc`'s non-blocking flock and the trash/grace discipline — they should be
verified rather than built.
